component.name: smpps
component.title: SMPP (Secure)
component.description: Send and receive SMS messages through an SMSC (Short Message Service Center) with the SMPP protocol.
component.label: mobile

initialReconnectDelay.label: common
initialReconnectDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds before the first attempt to reconnect, after the consumer or producer lost its session to the SMSC (the connection was closed, or the SMSC unbound). A failed connect when the consumer or producer starts is not retried.

maxReconnect.label: common
maxReconnect.description: The maximum number of attempts to reconnect after the session to the SMSC was lost. When the last attempt fails, a consumer stays disconnected until it is restarted, and a producer fails its exchanges, unless lazySessionCreation is enabled, which connects again for the next exchange.

reconnectDelay.label: common
reconnectDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds between two attempts to reconnect to the SMSC, after the first attempt failed.

splittingPolicy.description: What the producer does with a SubmitSm or SubmitMulti whose body does not fit in one short message: ALLOW sends it in several segments, TRUNCATE sends only its first part, and REJECT fails the exchange with an SmppException caused by a NegativeResponseException with status 1. Some carriers drop the segments after the first, which TRUNCATE does not send. The CamelSmppSplittingPolicy header replaces it.

systemType.label: common
systemType.description: The system_type of the bind request, which tells the SMSC the type of ESME (External Short Message Entity) that binds. SMPP 3.4 allows at most 13 octets, the NULL terminator included. Empty by default.

addressRange.label: consumer
addressRange.description: The address_range of the bind request of the consumer: the SME addresses that this ESME serves, as defined in section 5.2.7 of the SMPP 3.4 specification. The SMSC uses it to select the messages that it delivers to the consumer. Empty by default.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

destAddr.label: producer
destAddr.description: The destination address that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, for example the phone number of the recipient of a mobile terminated message. The CamelSmppDestAddr header replaces it, with a list of addresses for SubmitMulti.

destAddrNpi.label: producer
destAddrNpi.description: The numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the destination address that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, with the values of the sourceAddrNpi option. The CamelSmppDestAddrNpi header replaces it; the default is 0.

destAddrTon.label: producer
destAddrTon.description: The type of number (TON) of the destination address that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, with the values of the sourceAddrTon option. The CamelSmppDestAddrTon header replaces it; the default is 0.

lazySessionCreation.label: producer
lazySessionCreation.description: Whether the producer connects to the SMSC when it sends its first exchange instead of when it starts, so that the route can start while the SMSC is not available. The producer binds with the systemId and password options, or with headers when allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders is enabled.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

messageReceiverRouteId.label: producer
messageReceiverRouteId.description: The id of a route whose consumer receives the messages that the SMSC sends to this producer. The producer then binds as a transceiver (bind_transceiver) instead of a transmitter, and hands each received deliver_sm, data_sm and alert_notification to that route, so that no SMPP consumer is needed. Only tested with a route that starts from a direct endpoint; the route must exist when Camel starts.

numberingPlanIndicator.label: producer
numberingPlanIndicator.description: The numbering plan indicator (NPI) that the producer sends in the addr_npi field of its bind request, with the values of the sourceAddrNpi option. The consumer binds with 0 (unknown). The default is 0.

priorityFlag.label: producer
priorityFlag.description: The priority_flag that the producer sends with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, from 0 (lowest) to 3 (highest). The CamelSmppPriorityFlag header replaces it; the default is 1.

protocolId.label: producer
protocolId.description: The protocol_id that the producer sends with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which for GSM is set as defined in GSM 03.40. The CamelSmppProtocolId header replaces it; the default is 0.

registeredDelivery.label: producer
registeredDelivery.description: The registered_delivery that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, ReplaceSm and DataSm: 0 requests no delivery receipt, 1 a delivery receipt for success and for failure, and 2 a delivery receipt for failure only. The CamelSmppRegisteredDelivery header replaces it; the default is 1.

replaceIfPresentFlag.label: producer
replaceIfPresentFlag.description: The replace_if_present_flag that the producer sends with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti: 1 asks the SMSC to replace a message that is still pending delivery and has the same source address, destination address and service type, 0 does not. The CamelSmppReplaceIfPresentFlag header replaces it; the default is 0.

serviceType.label: producer
serviceType.description: The service_type that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm: the SMS application service of the message, such as CMT (cellular messaging), CPT (cellular paging), VMN (voice mail notification), VMA (voice mail alerting), WAP or USSD. Empty by default, for the default service of the SMSC. The CamelSmppServiceType header replaces it.

sourceAddr.label: producer
sourceAddr.description: The source address that the producer sends with every command: the address of the SME (Short Message Entity) that sends the message, or, for ReplaceSm, QuerySm and CancelSm, the source address of the original message. The CamelSmppSourceAddr header replaces it.

sourceAddrNpi.label: producer
sourceAddrNpi.description: The numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the source address that the producer sends with every command: 0 unknown, 1 ISDN (E.163/E.164), 2 data (X.121), 3 telex (F.69), 6 land mobile (E.212), 8 national, 9 private, 10 ERMES, 13 Internet (IP) or 18 WAP client id. The CamelSmppSourceAddrNpi header replaces it; the default is 0.

sourceAddrTon.label: producer
sourceAddrTon.description: The type of number (TON) of the source address that the producer sends with every command: 0 unknown, 1 international, 2 national, 3 network specific, 4 subscriber number, 5 alphanumeric or 6 abbreviated. The CamelSmppSourceAddrTon header replaces it; the default is 0.

typeOfNumber.label: producer
typeOfNumber.description: The type of number (TON) that the producer sends in the addr_ton field of its bind request, with the values of the sourceAddrTon option. The consumer binds with 0 (unknown). The default is 0.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

configuration.label: advanced
configuration.description: A shared SmppConfiguration as the base of the endpoints: each endpoint uses a copy of it, which the options of its URI change.

enquireLinkTimer.label: advanced
enquireLinkTimer.description: The time in milliseconds without data from the SMSC after which the session sends an enquire_link to check the connection, or 0 to send none. Camel also uses it as the timeout to connect to the SMSC or the HTTP proxy, and for the TLS handshake.

interfaceVersion.label: advanced
interfaceVersion.description: Defines the interface version to be used in the binding request with the SMSC. The following values are allowed, as defined in the SMPP protocol (and the underlying implementation using the jSMPP library, respectively): legacy (0x00), 3.3 (0x33), 3.4 (0x34), and 5.0 (0x50). The default (fallback) value is version 3.4.

pduProcessorDegree.label: advanced
pduProcessorDegree.description: The number of threads of the SMPP session that process the received PDUs in parallel.

pduProcessorQueueCapacity.label: advanced
pduProcessorQueueCapacity.description: The number of received PDUs that can wait for a free processing thread. When the queue is full, the session answers a received request with the ESME_RTHROTTLED error, so that the SMSC slows down.

sessionStateListener.label: advanced
sessionStateListener.description: An org.jsmpp.session.SessionStateListener that is notified when the state of the SMPP session of the consumer or producer changes, for example from BOUND_RX to CLOSED. Camel still reconnects a lost session itself.

singleDLR.label: advanced
singleDLR.description: When true, the SMSC delivery receipt would be requested only for the last segment of a multi-segment (long) message. For short messages, with only 1 segment the behaviour is unchanged.

transactionTimer.label: advanced
transactionTimer.description: The time in milliseconds that the session waits for the response of the SMSC to a request that it sent, such as a submit_sm or an enquire_link, before the request fails. The bind request waits 60 seconds instead.

alphabet.label: codec
alphabet.description: The alphabet in which the producer encodes and splits the text of the short message for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm: 0 (the SMSC default alphabet) encodes it in the charset of the encoding option, 8 (UCS2) in UTF-16BE, and 4 (8-bit) sends a byte array body as it is. It does not set the data_coding that is sent, which comes from the dataCoding option. The CamelSmppAlphabet header replaces it; the default is 0.

dataCoding.label: codec
dataCoding.description: The data_coding that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm, as defined in section 5.2.19 of the SMPP 3.4 specification, for example 0 for the SMSC default alphabet, 3 for Latin 1, 4 for 8-bit binary data and 8 for UCS2. An 8-bit value sends a byte array body as it is; the alphabet and encoding options, not this option, select how a text body is encoded. The CamelSmppDataCoding and CamelSmppAlphabet headers replace it; the default is 0.

encoding.label: codec
encoding.description: The charset in which the producer encodes the text of the short message for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm, unless the alphabet is UCS2, and in which the consumer decodes a received message in the SMSC default alphabet. The CamelSmppEncoding header replaces it for the producer.

httpProxyHost.label: proxy
httpProxyHost.description: The host name or IP address of an HTTP proxy through which Camel tunnels the SMPP connection, with an HTTP CONNECT request. When not set, Camel connects to the SMSC directly.

httpProxyPassword.label: proxy
httpProxyPassword.description: The password for Basic authentication with the HTTP proxy. It is sent only together with the httpProxyUsername option.

httpProxyPort.label: proxy
httpProxyPort.description: The port of the HTTP proxy that the httpProxyHost option sets.

httpProxyUsername.label: proxy
httpProxyUsername.description: The user name for Basic authentication with the HTTP proxy. It is sent only together with the httpProxyPassword option.

proxyHeaders.label: proxy
proxyHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers that Camel sends to the HTTP proxy with the CONNECT request.

allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.displayName: Allow System Id And Password From Headers
allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.label: producer,security
allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.description: Whether a producer with lazySessionCreation=true may take the system id and the password, with which it connects to the SMSC, from the 'CamelSmppSystemId' and 'CamelSmppPassword' headers of the first exchange. When both headers are present, the producer connects with them in place of the systemId and password of the endpoint, and keeps using them when it reconnects. This is disabled by default, and the headers are then ignored. Enable this only when the route sets these headers itself.

hostnameVerification.label: security
hostnameVerification.description: Whether to check that the certificate of the SMSC matches the host Camel connects to, when SSL is used. When disabled, any certificate trusted by the JVM is accepted, whatever host it was issued for.

password.label: security
password.description: The password with which the consumer or producer binds to the SMSC.

systemId.label: security
systemId.description: The system_id with which the consumer or producer binds to the SMSC: the user name that the SMSC authenticates. The user info of the URI, as in smpp://userhost, sets it too.

usingSSL.label: security
usingSSL.description: Whether to connect to the SMSC with TLS, which the smpps scheme enables. The certificate of the SMSC must be trusted by the default SSL socket factory of the JVM. Through an HTTP proxy, TLS runs inside the tunnel.

CamelSmppAlphabet.label: producer
CamelSmppAlphabet.description: The alphabet of the short message, which replaces the alphabet option for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm: 0 for the SMSC default alphabet, 4 for 8-bit data and 8 for UCS2. When the CamelSmppDataCoding header is not set, SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm also send it as the data_coding.

CamelSmppCommand.description: The command to send: SubmitSm (the default when the header is missing), ReplaceSm, QuerySm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm or DataSm. The names are case-sensitive, and any other value fails.

CamelSmppCommandId.label: consumer
CamelSmppCommandId.description: The command_id of the received PDU, which identifies its type, as listed in section 5.1.2.1 of the SMPP 3.4 specification. Set for an AlertNotification, a DeliverSm and a DataSm.

CamelSmppCommandStatus.label: consumer
CamelSmppCommandStatus.description: The command_status of the received PDU. Set for an AlertNotification and a DataSm.

CamelSmppDataCoding.label: producer
CamelSmppDataCoding.description: For the producer, the data_coding to send with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm, which replaces the dataCoding option; with an 8-bit value, the body is sent as bytes, for ReplaceSm too. The consumer sets it to the data_coding of a received DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppSplitter.label: producer
CamelSmppSplitter.description: An org.apache.camel.component.smpp.SmppSplitter that splits the body into segments for SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, instead of the splitter that the producer chooses for the alphabet. A value that is not an SmppSplitter fails the exchange.

CamelSmppDelivered.label: consumer
CamelSmppDelivered.description: The number of short messages delivered, from the dlvrd field of a delivery receipt. It is relevant only when the original message was submitted to a distribution list.

CamelSmppDestAddr.description: For the producer, the destination address for SubmitSm, CancelSm and DataSm, or a list of destination addresses for SubmitMulti, which replaces the destAddr option. The consumer sets it to the destination address of a received DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppDestAddrNpi.description: For the producer, the numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the destination address for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, which replaces the destAddrNpi option. The consumer sets it to the NPI of the destination address of a received DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppDestAddrTon.description: For the producer, the type of number (TON) of the destination address for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, which replaces the destAddrTon option. The consumer sets it to the TON of the destination address of a received DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppDoneDate.label: consumer
CamelSmppDoneDate.description: The date and time at which the message reached its final state, from the done date field of a delivery receipt.

CamelSmppEncoding.label: producer
CamelSmppEncoding.description: The charset in which the producer encodes the text of the body for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm, which replaces the encoding option, also for the UCS2 alphabet. A charset that the JVM does not support is logged and ignored. It is not used for an 8-bit message, whose body is sent as bytes: a byte array as it is, any other body converted in the charset of the exchange.

CamelSmppError.description: The producer sets it for SubmitMulti, when some destinations failed, to a map from the message id to a list of maps, each with the destination address (CamelSmppDestAddr key) and the error code (CamelSmppError key); for QuerySm, it sets it to the error_code of the response. The consumer sets it to the err field of a delivery receipt, a network or SMSC specific error code, when it is not 000.

CamelSmppClass.label: producer
CamelSmppClass.description: The esm_class to send with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti. Without it, the producer sends the default esm_class, or the one with the UDH indicator for a message that it splits.

CamelSmppEsmeAddr.label: consumer
CamelSmppEsmeAddr.description: The esme_addr of a received AlertNotification: the address of the ESME that requested the alert.

CamelSmppEsmeAddrNpi.label: consumer
CamelSmppEsmeAddrNpi.description: The numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the esme_addr of a received AlertNotification.

CamelSmppEsmeAddrTon.label: consumer
CamelSmppEsmeAddrTon.description: The type of number (TON) of the esme_addr of a received AlertNotification.

CamelSmppFinalDate.label: producer
CamelSmppFinalDate.description: The date and time at which the message reached its final state, from the final_date of the response to QuerySm, or null when the message has not reached a final state.

CamelSmppStatus.label: consumer
CamelSmppStatus.description: The final state of the message, from the stat field of a delivery receipt, such as DELIVRD, UNDELIV or EXPIRED.

CamelSmppId.description: For ReplaceSm, QuerySm and CancelSm, the message id of the message to act on, as the SMSC returned it. After the send, the producer sets it to the list of message ids that the SMSC returned for SubmitSm and SubmitMulti (one per segment), and to a single message id for the other commands. The consumer sets it to the id of the original message for a delivery receipt, and to the message id that it returns to the SMSC for a DataSm.

CamelSmppMessageState.label: producer
CamelSmppMessageState.description: The state of the message from the response to QuerySm, as the name of an org.jsmpp.bean.MessageState, such as ENROUTE, DELIVERED or EXPIRED.

CamelSmppMessageType.label: consumer
CamelSmppMessageType.description: Identifies the type of an incoming message: AlertNotification: an SMSC alert notification, DataSm: an SMSC data short message, DeliveryReceipt: an SMSC delivery receipt, DeliverSm: an SMSC deliver short message

CamelSmppPriorityFlag.label: producer
CamelSmppPriorityFlag.description: The priority_flag to send with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, from 0 (lowest) to 3 (highest), which replaces the priorityFlag option.

CamelSmppProtocolId.label: producer
CamelSmppProtocolId.description: The protocol_id to send with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which replaces the protocolId option.

CamelSmppRegisteredDelivery.description: For the producer, the registered_delivery to send with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, ReplaceSm and DataSm, which replaces the registeredDelivery option. The consumer sets it to the registered_delivery of a received DataSm.

CamelSmppSingleDLR.label: producer
CamelSmppSingleDLR.description: Whether to request a delivery receipt only for the last segment of a message that is split, for SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which replaces the singleDLR option.

CamelSmppReplaceIfPresentFlag.label: producer
CamelSmppReplaceIfPresentFlag.description: The replace_if_present_flag to send with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which replaces the replaceIfPresentFlag option: 1 asks the SMSC to replace a message that is still pending delivery and has the same source address, destination address and service type, 0 does not.

CamelSmppScheduleDeliveryTime.description: For the producer, the time at which the SMSC first tries to deliver the message, for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm, as a java.util.Date that is sent in the absolute time format of the SMPP 3.4 specification, section 7.1.1. The consumer sets it to the schedule_delivery_time of a received DeliverSm, as the String in that format.

CamelSmppSentMessageCount.label: producer
CamelSmppSentMessageCount.description: The number of short messages that the producer sent for SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which is more than one when the body was split.

CamelSmppSequenceNumber.label: consumer
CamelSmppSequenceNumber.description: The sequence_number of the received PDU, which correlates the response with the request. Set for an AlertNotification, a DeliverSm and a DataSm.

CamelSmppServiceType.description: For the producer, the service_type to send with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm, which replaces the serviceType option. The consumer sets it to the service_type of a received DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppSourceAddr.description: For the producer, the source address to send with every command, which replaces the sourceAddr option; for ReplaceSm, QuerySm and CancelSm, the source address of the original message. The consumer sets it to the source address of a received AlertNotification, DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppSourceAddrNpi.description: For the producer, the numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the source address to send with every command, which replaces the sourceAddrNpi option. The consumer sets it to the NPI of the source address of a received AlertNotification, DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppSourceAddrTon.description: For the producer, the type of number (TON) of the source address to send with every command, which replaces the sourceAddrTon option. The consumer sets it to the TON of the source address of a received AlertNotification, DeliverSm or DataSm.

CamelSmppSubmitted.label: consumer
CamelSmppSubmitted.description: The number of short messages originally submitted, from the sub field of a delivery receipt. It is relevant only when the original message was submitted to a distribution list.

CamelSmppSubmitDate.label: consumer
CamelSmppSubmitDate.description: The date and time at which the original message was submitted, or replaced, from the submit date field of a delivery receipt.

CamelSmppSystemId.label: producer
CamelSmppSystemId.description: The system id to connect to the SMSC with. Used only by the first exchange of a producer with lazySessionCreation=true and allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders=true, together with the CamelSmppPassword header; otherwise ignored.

CamelSmppPassword.label: producer
CamelSmppPassword.description: The password to connect to the SMSC with. Used only by the first exchange of a producer with lazySessionCreation=true and allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders=true, together with the CamelSmppSystemId header; otherwise ignored.

CamelSmppValidityPeriod.description: For the producer, the time after which the SMSC discards the message if it was not delivered, for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm: a java.util.Date is sent in the absolute time format, and a String as it is, so it can hold a relative time (SMPP 3.4 specification, section 7.1.1). The consumer sets it to the validity_period of a received DeliverSm, as a String.

CamelSmppOptionalParameters.label: consumer
CamelSmppOptionalParameters.description: The optional parameters (TLVs) by the name of their org.jsmpp.bean.OptionalParameter.Tag. The producer sends them, with String values, with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm when the CamelSmppOptionalParameter header is not set. The consumer sets it for a received DeliverSm, and the producer for the response to DataSm. Deprecation note: Use CamelSmppOptionalParameter instead

CamelSmppOptionalParameter.description: The optional parameters (TLVs) by their tag code. The producer sends them with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm: a String as a COctetString, a byte array as an OctetString, a Byte, a Short or an Integer as a parameter of that size, and null as a parameter without value; it skips other values. The consumer sets it for a received DeliverSm, and the producer for the response to DataSm, with the values converted back the same way.

CamelSmppSplittingPolicy.label: producer
CamelSmppSplittingPolicy.description: The splitting policy for SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, ALLOW, REJECT or TRUNCATE, which replaces the splittingPolicy option. Any other value fails the exchange.

consumerOut.description: A short message as text decoded by its data coding, or as bytes for an 8-bit data coding; the text of a delivery receipt, with its fields in headers. A data_sm or an alert notification has no body

producerIn.description: The text of the short message: bytes, a stream or a file are read as text, unless an 8-bit CamelSmppDataCoding or CamelSmppAlphabet header, or an 8-bit dataCoding or alphabet option for a byte array, sends bytes as they are. A stream is read once and replaced by its content. No body fails; a Map or a POJO is sent as its toString(). DataSm, QuerySm and CancelSm do not read the body

producerOut.description: Unchanged, with the message ids in the CamelSmppId header, also when the exchange expects a reply (InOut)

host.description: The host name or IP address of the SMSC.

port.description: The TCP port of the SMSC.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

protocolId.description: The protocol_id that the producer sends with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti, which for GSM is set as defined in GSM 03.40. The CamelSmppProtocolId header replaces it; the default is 0.

registeredDelivery.label: producer
registeredDelivery.description: The registered_delivery that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, ReplaceSm and DataSm: 0 requests no delivery receipt, 1 a delivery receipt for success and for failure, and 2 a delivery receipt for failure only. The CamelSmppRegisteredDelivery header replaces it; the default is 1.

replaceIfPresentFlag.label: producer
replaceIfPresentFlag.description: The replace_if_present_flag that the producer sends with SubmitSm and SubmitMulti: 1 asks the SMSC to replace a message that is still pending delivery and has the same source address, destination address and service type, 0 does not. The CamelSmppReplaceIfPresentFlag header replaces it; the default is 0.

serviceType.label: producer
serviceType.description: The service_type that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti, CancelSm and DataSm: the SMS application service of the message, such as CMT (cellular messaging), CPT (cellular paging), VMN (voice mail notification), VMA (voice mail alerting), WAP or USSD. Empty by default, for the default service of the SMSC. The CamelSmppServiceType header replaces it.

sourceAddr.label: producer
sourceAddr.description: The source address that the producer sends with every command: the address of the SME (Short Message Entity) that sends the message, or, for ReplaceSm, QuerySm and CancelSm, the source address of the original message. The CamelSmppSourceAddr header replaces it.

sourceAddrNpi.label: producer
sourceAddrNpi.description: The numbering plan indicator (NPI) of the source address that the producer sends with every command: 0 unknown, 1 ISDN (E.163/E.164), 2 data (X.121), 3 telex (F.69), 6 land mobile (E.212), 8 national, 9 private, 10 ERMES, 13 Internet (IP) or 18 WAP client id. The CamelSmppSourceAddrNpi header replaces it; the default is 0.

sourceAddrTon.label: producer
sourceAddrTon.description: The type of number (TON) of the source address that the producer sends with every command: 0 unknown, 1 international, 2 national, 3 network specific, 4 subscriber number, 5 alphanumeric or 6 abbreviated. The CamelSmppSourceAddrTon header replaces it; the default is 0.

typeOfNumber.label: producer
typeOfNumber.description: The type of number (TON) that the producer sends in the addr_ton field of its bind request, with the values of the sourceAddrTon option. The consumer binds with 0 (unknown). The default is 0.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

enquireLinkTimer.label: advanced
enquireLinkTimer.description: The time in milliseconds without data from the SMSC after which the session sends an enquire_link to check the connection, or 0 to send none. Camel also uses it as the timeout to connect to the SMSC or the HTTP proxy, and for the TLS handshake.

interfaceVersion.label: advanced
interfaceVersion.description: Defines the interface version to be used in the binding request with the SMSC. The following values are allowed, as defined in the SMPP protocol (and the underlying implementation using the jSMPP library, respectively): legacy (0x00), 3.3 (0x33), 3.4 (0x34), and 5.0 (0x50). The default (fallback) value is version 3.4.

pduProcessorDegree.label: advanced
pduProcessorDegree.description: The number of threads of the SMPP session that process the received PDUs in parallel.

pduProcessorQueueCapacity.label: advanced
pduProcessorQueueCapacity.description: The number of received PDUs that can wait for a free processing thread. When the queue is full, the session answers a received request with the ESME_RTHROTTLED error, so that the SMSC slows down.

sessionStateListener.label: advanced
sessionStateListener.description: An org.jsmpp.session.SessionStateListener that is notified when the state of the SMPP session of the consumer or producer changes, for example from BOUND_RX to CLOSED. Camel still reconnects a lost session itself.

singleDLR.label: advanced
singleDLR.description: When true, the SMSC delivery receipt would be requested only for the last segment of a multi-segment (long) message. For short messages, with only 1 segment the behaviour is unchanged.

transactionTimer.label: advanced
transactionTimer.description: The time in milliseconds that the session waits for the response of the SMSC to a request that it sent, such as a submit_sm or an enquire_link, before the request fails. The bind request waits 60 seconds instead.

alphabet.label: codec
alphabet.description: The alphabet in which the producer encodes and splits the text of the short message for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm: 0 (the SMSC default alphabet) encodes it in the charset of the encoding option, 8 (UCS2) in UTF-16BE, and 4 (8-bit) sends a byte array body as it is. It does not set the data_coding that is sent, which comes from the dataCoding option. The CamelSmppAlphabet header replaces it; the default is 0.

dataCoding.label: codec
dataCoding.description: The data_coding that the producer sends with SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and DataSm, as defined in section 5.2.19 of the SMPP 3.4 specification, for example 0 for the SMSC default alphabet, 3 for Latin 1, 4 for 8-bit binary data and 8 for UCS2. An 8-bit value sends a byte array body as it is; the alphabet and encoding options, not this option, select how a text body is encoded. The CamelSmppDataCoding and CamelSmppAlphabet headers replace it; the default is 0.

encoding.label: codec
encoding.description: The charset in which the producer encodes the text of the short message for SubmitSm, SubmitMulti and ReplaceSm, unless the alphabet is UCS2, and in which the consumer decodes a received message in the SMSC default alphabet. The CamelSmppEncoding header replaces it for the producer.

httpProxyHost.label: proxy
httpProxyHost.description: The host name or IP address of an HTTP proxy through which Camel tunnels the SMPP connection, with an HTTP CONNECT request. When not set, Camel connects to the SMSC directly.

httpProxyPassword.label: proxy
httpProxyPassword.description: The password for Basic authentication with the HTTP proxy. It is sent only together with the httpProxyUsername option.

httpProxyPort.label: proxy
httpProxyPort.description: The port of the HTTP proxy that the httpProxyHost option sets.

httpProxyUsername.label: proxy
httpProxyUsername.description: The user name for Basic authentication with the HTTP proxy. It is sent only together with the httpProxyPassword option.

proxyHeaders.label: proxy
proxyHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers that Camel sends to the HTTP proxy with the CONNECT request.

allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.displayName: Allow System Id And Password From Headers
allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.label: producer,security
allowSystemIdAndPasswordFromHeaders.description: Whether a producer with lazySessionCreation=true may take the system id and the password, with which it connects to the SMSC, from the 'CamelSmppSystemId' and 'CamelSmppPassword' headers of the first exchange. When both headers are present, the producer connects with them in place of the systemId and password of the endpoint, and keeps using them when it reconnects. This is disabled by default, and the headers are then ignored. Enable this only when the route sets these headers itself.

hostnameVerification.label: security
hostnameVerification.description: Whether to check that the certificate of the SMSC matches the host Camel connects to, when SSL is used. When disabled, any certificate trusted by the JVM is accepted, whatever host it was issued for.

password.label: security
password.description: The password with which the consumer or producer binds to the SMSC.

systemId.label: security
systemId.description: The system_id with which the consumer or producer binds to the SMSC: the user name that the SMSC authenticates. The user info of the URI, as in smpp://userhost, sets it too.

usingSSL.label: security
usingSSL.description: Whether to connect to the SMSC with TLS, which the smpps scheme enables. The certificate of the SMSC must be trusted by the default SSL socket factory of the JVM. Through an HTTP proxy, TLS runs inside the tunnel.
